note: FIXTURE for L25: shaped like `pip-audit --format json` output so you can practise triage offline. The CVE ids, affected packages and fix versions are real public advisories (checked 2026-10); the descriptions are paraphrased. LAB-2026-0042 is invented for the lab and is not a real advisory. The scan ran against an OLDER lock file than the one in work/patch/report/requirements.txt (compare scanner.lock_sha256), as scans in a release queue often do.

vulns.description: idna.encode() can take quadratic time on specially crafted input strings, so an attacker who controls the string being encoded can cause a denial of service (CPU exhaustion).

The xmlattr filter accepted keys containing characters such as '/', '>' and '=' that are not valid in attribute names; if an application passes user-controlled keys to xmlattr, other attributes can be injected (XSS).
A bug in the template compiler lets an attacker who controls BOTH the content and the filename of a template execute arbitrary Python code, regardless of whether the sandbox is used.
The sandboxed environment did not detect indirect calls to str.format, so an attacker who controls the content of a template rendered in the sandbox can execute arbitrary Python code.
The sandboxed environment's interaction with the |attr filter allows an attacker who controls the content of a template rendered in the sandbox to execute arbitrary Python code.
Internal review note (invented for this lab): 'the --out directory handling may allow writing outside the intended directory'. Not reproduced, no fix version, owner not yet assigned.
